task: Apply Biel 3's second independent review correction to the existing Core project responsible-assignment patch. The new project UI link is fixed and names PROJECT_OWNER_ACCESS_CHANGE, but the administrative elevation form still defaults to ACCOUNT_APPLICATION_REVIEW, so the supported path remains error-prone and the production evidence showed no elevation-start/activation before failed assignment attempts. Make the fixed internal project link safely preselect PROJECT_OWNER_ACCESS_CHANGE in the existing admin elevation form, validating any query value against UI_ELEVATION_SCOPES and preserving the default for direct generic admin visits; do not add an arbitrary return URL or bypass elevation. Keep the existing Cloudflare -> CSRF -> session -> OWNER authorization -> scoped elevation -> serializable mutation ordering. Make the wrapper regression test runnable under the repository's normal tsx test setup (avoid unsupported top-level-await/CJS invocation), include it in the focused Core unit command or existing DB suite without broad infrastructure, and prove the actual setCoreProjectAccess Server Action wrapper plus persisted/read-back behavior. Do not weaken invalid/expired elevation, target, authorization, isolation, or last-owner protections. Preserve all nine pre-existing unrelated dirty WIP paths exactly. No dependencies, commit, push, publication, deploy, restart, or production data mutation. Run focused tests, DB integration, typecheck/lint where feasible, and git diff --check; return the exact structured executor JSON report.
constraints: Biel 4 remains Executor only; do not issue an Architect review or acceptance verdict.
Use only the same configured Biel4 App Server/headless executor with task_transport=app_server. No native subagents, create_thread, TUI fallback, codex exec, or alternate backend.
Preserve the nine pre-existing unrelated WIP paths exactly; do not reset, clean, stash-drop, amend, rebase, or rewrite them.
Do not expose .env, credentials, cookies, session tokens, JWTs, passwords, recovery codes, raw identifiers, private logs, or database dumps.
No commit, push, PR, merge, tag, release, deploy, production rebuild/restart, Cloudflare/DNS mutation, or destructive database action.

review_findings.title: Blocking: required scope is not selected by the fixed project flow
review_findings.details: The project access panel links to /core/security/admin#admin-elevation-form and explains PROJECT_OWNER_ACCESS_CHANGE, but AdminSecurityPanel still defaults the scope select to UI_ELEVATION_SCOPES[0] (ACCOUNT_APPLICATION_REVIEW). A user following the supported link can submit the wrong elevation and the later guarded assignment must fail. Use a fixed internal query scope, validate it against the allowlisted UI scopes, and default only that scoped entry while preserving generic direct visits.

review_findings.title: Blocking: the new wrapper regression is not runnable by the recorded command
review_findings.details: The wrapper test uses top-level await and fails under the repository's normal CJS tsx test setup with 'Top-level await is currently not supported with the cjs output format'. It is also absent from test:core:unit. Repair the test harness with existing test conventions and wire it into a focused suite so the actual Next Server Action wrapper is exercised, not only the injected helper.
